description: Cap recount parity cases (spec 9.3), shared by the daemon (test_coadaptation_engine.py) and the UI reducer (commitRules.test.ts). Each block has an interruption cap (null = none), whether pin_act is active, and trials in order. A trial lists reducer inputs in order: activations and trial-level events (veto, refresh). An activation names its governing regime (the trial's cue-time regime, or the revert regime from the revert on), whether A_gate > tau, whether it has a literal hit, n_plausible, whether the hit is irreversible (rule C9), whether the response comes from a pin_act collapse, the L2 response the table draw or the fixed rule would give before the cap rule (null when the activation is not routed to L2), and what happened next. expected.k_before is the block's count k before the activation (an idle epoch counts from 0 on its own); expected.result is the immediate response (set once), expected.outcome the final outcome, expected.source and expected.variant the applied L2 response (null when none). L1 confirm and hold steps count at most once per trial; L2 confirm steps, C9 confirm steps and clarification prompts count each time; the count reads result, never outcome.

blocks.description: L1 confirm regime: a cancelled confirm step, then a re-confirm in the same trial (adds 1 once)
Hold regime: an early release then a re-hold (adds 1 once); an aborted hold then a re-hold
Clarification answered 'None of these', then a second prompt answered with a choice (each adds 1)
Act-guarded trial with two L2 confirm steps and two clarification prompts (each adds 1)
Cap 2: once two steps are used, later ambiguous activations get wait_for_evidence (source cap)
Cap 1: wait_for_evidence from the table adds nothing; the cap applies after one prompt
C9 confirm steps on an irreversible literal hit count each time (cancelled, then confirmed)
pin_act collapse at the cap (cap 0): act on a hit, wait_for_evidence without one, never cap
A confirm step still open at the trial limit counts (outcome open_at_end)
A trial reverted from one confirm regime to another ('Not this time'; plain is hold_700): adds 1
Cap 8 under hold_700 with an early release and a re-hold in every trial: k reaches 8 after trial 8
An interrupted trial's steps count toward the block's k (cap 3)
An idle epoch counts from 0 on its own and uses the fixed L2 rule (cap 1)
assistance_off: commits and activations without a hit add nothing (cap 0)
Cap 0 in an act-guarded block: every ambiguous activation gets the cap response
A refresh under a new freeze keeps act; responses after the revert use the fixed L2 rule
An L2 'Not this time' reverts the trial to the plain regime (no L2 after the revert)
The cap is reached inside a trial by a cancelled L2 confirm; the next ambiguous activation gets cap
Hold regime under a cap of 2 (minimum caution keeps it): a no-hit activation adds nothing; an aborted hold and its re-hold add 1 once; k may pass the cap because an L1 regime is never capped
Three plausible candidates: ask_clarification:3 from the table, then a C9 confirm, then the cap
